MINUTES

  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION

  MARCH 13, 2018

An adjourned regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 3:05 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR
HUFF.

2.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell*, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.
  *Arrived at 3:20 p.m.
City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Todd Litfin, Rutan & Tucker, LLP addressed the City Council to provide an update on a matter of
litigation between his client, Dr. Hendrik Baars, D.D.S. (tenant) and SRE DCM PV, LLC (property
owner) regarding use of a property located at 27520 Hawthorne Blvd., Rolling Hills Estates
(Peninsula Pointe).

4.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  MID-YEAR REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE MID-YEAR REPORTS.

  THERE BEING NO OBJCTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 13, 2018 (POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION)
 B.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the items presented and prioritize
  them on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

  CITY MANAGER

  CITY PROSECUTOR

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) and provided
  the background on the City’s relationship with the firm currently providing prosecution
  services, Jones & Mayer. He noted that given the City Attorney’s familiarity with the
  City’s municipal code and daily operations, it makes sense, from a cost/operational
  standpoint, to have the City Attorney’s office begin providing prosecution services
  effective July 1, 2018.

  Discussion ensued concerning the City’s relationship with Marty Mayer and the City
  Council expressed sincere respect for Mr. Mayer and appreciation for the services Mr.
  Mayer’s firm provided over the years.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to move
  forward in having the City Attorney’s office begin handling prosecution services effective
  July 1, 2018.

  COUNCIL COMMUNICATION

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that she found the committee
  communication/transition process very useful as the committees were reorganized.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

  PUBLIC OUTREACH: Communications

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material)
  and reviewed the background on this matter. She further provided a summary of the
  City’s communication plan being developing in conjunction with Tripepi Smith, the
  consultant retained to work with the City to further the public engagement. Ryder Smith
  with Tripepi Smith further reviewed the Communications and Public Engagement Plan
  Report.

  Discussion ensued concerning the importance of public engagement and the options for
  moving forward to enhance public engagement.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to identify
  a scope of work for enhancing public engagement, to be divided in to levels of support,
  and return with a cost proposal for such services.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 13, 2018 (POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION)
   PUBLIC OUTREACH: Emergency Communications

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material)
  and reviewed the various options available for emergency communication.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to proceed
  with budgeting for the Nixle 360 emergency alert system and bring back cost information
  to the City Council at the Budget Study Session.

  PUBLIC OUTREACH: Agenda Engagement

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material)
  noting that the City’s current agenda management platform offers an option to allow e-
  comments.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to not move forward with
  this option.

  PUBLIC OUTREACH: E-mail Campaign Options

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material)
  and reviewed several option available for e-mail campaigns and the costs associated
  with each option.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to move
  forward with using Constant Contact as an e-mail campaign provider and to analyze the
  results after a year to determine effectiveness.

  PUBLIC SAFETY: Coyote Management

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material)
  and briefly reviewed the City’s current Coyote Management Plan.

  Gordon Ramsbottom of the Rancho Palomino Neighborhood addressed the City Council
  to encourage the City to pursue further more aggressive efforts in regard to coyote
  management and suggested that a mailer be sent to the entire city to inform the
  residents about coyote management.

  Discussion ensued concerning the public safety threat coyotes present and the options
  available for coyote management including trapping and direct suppression on certain
  areas of public property.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  administratively work the County of Los Angeles to pursue further coyote management
  options including trapping and direct suppression on public property. Staff was further
  directed to prepare an informational flyer on coyote management to be mailed to all
  households in the City.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 13, 2018 (POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION)
   PUBLIC SAFETY: Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) Cameras / Security Cameras
  for Home Owners Associations (HOA’s)

  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material.) She reviewed the locations where the ALPR cameras are currently located in
  the city along with proposed options for adding ALPR camera.

  Discussion ensued concerning the current and proposed locations of the ALPR cameras
  and the possibility of locating ALPR cameras at specific neighborhood entrances.
  Recognizing that is it not feasible or cost effective to place ALPR cameras at a specific
  neighborhood entrance, further discussion ensued concerning the possibility of the City
  providing some level of grant funding for HOA’s to purchase and install approved
  security/surveillance cameras at their neighborhood entrances.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to proceed
  with budgeting for the ALPR cameras in the locations proposed (both direction) and
  bring back cost estimates to the City Council at the Budget Study Session. Staff was
  further directed to further research the options for providing funding for HOA’s to
  purchase and install approved security/surveillance cameras at their neighborhood
  entrances and return with a proposal.

  EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS: Horses

  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material.)

  Following discussion, it wat the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to move
  forward in working with the Los Angeles County Equine Response Team to develop a
  horse census for the City.

  EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS: Torrance Refinery

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material)
  noting that it was suggested a recent Neighborhood Watch meeting that the City take a
  position of opposition with regard to the Torrance Refinery.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to not take a position.

  PLANNING DIRECTOR

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) including
  an update on the status of the General Plan Advisory Committee and California Water
  Service Company’s Palos Verdes Peninsula Water Reliability Project.

  Discussion ensued concerning the Cal Water project and in response to an inquiry
  regarding the City’s ability to require specie earthquake resistant pipes, the City
  Attorney was asked to research the matter further.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 13, 2018 (POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION)
   ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIRECTOR

  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW

  City Manager Prichard reviewed the City’s projected revenue and expenditures including
  expected exceptional revenue over the next several years, the CalPERS Unfunded
  Accrued Liability (UAL) and upcoming public works projects including the proposed City
  Hall/Council Chambers renovation project.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead reviewed several scenarios for paying down
  the CalPERS UAL using an interactive spreadsheet that showed the impact of the
  various scenarios on the principal and interest.

  Mark Young, KNN Public Finance reviewed the City’s financial position including the
  reserve policy and discussed the options for paying down the CalPERS UAL and funding
  the various public works project.

  It was the consensus of the City Council to proceed with the Council Chambers
  renovation portion of City Hall renovation project.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to further
  analyze the options available for paying down the CalPERS UAL and funding upcoming
  public works projects, including the options of tax exempt borrowing for capital projects;
  and present the options to the City Council at the Budget Study Session.

  COMMUNITY SERVICES DIRECTOR

  CITY FACILITY NAMING POLICY

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the City develop a policy for the naming
  of city facilities. He suggested that if a facility is to be named after an individual that it
  would have more impact and meaning if it was done before they passed away.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to research
  facility naming policies and return to the City Council with options.

  PROPOSED DOG PARK

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to research
  the options for pursuing a dog park, possibly on County land, and present the options
  to the Park and Activities Commission for discussion and consideration.

  SISTER CITY

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to not participate in the
  Sister City program.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 13, 2018 (POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION)
   CITY CELEBRATION

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council that the City Celebration
  be moved back to the Empty Saddle Club.

  Following discussion on the matters above, MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved,
  seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE POLICY DEVEOPMENT SESSION REPORTS WITH
  DIRECTION TO STAFF AS NOTED FOR EACH ITEM ABOVE.

  THERE BEING NO OBJCTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED

5.  CLOSED SESSION

Closed session taken out of order. The City Council recessed into closed session at 5:09 p.m.
Adjourned closed session at 5:55 p.m. and meeting reconvened in Open Session

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: Administrative Analyst

  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR
  Government Code Section 54957.6
  City representative: City Manager
  Unrepresented employee: Planning Technician/Code Administrator

  STAFF WAS DIRECTED TO PREPARE RESOLUTIONS FOR COUNCIL
  CONSIDERATION TO ESTABLISH A FULL TIME CODE ENFORCMENT POSITION
  AND AN ADMINISTRATIVE ANALYST POSITION.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:10 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular
  meeting of the City Council scheduled for on Tuesday, March 27, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in
  the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 13, 2018 (POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION)
